30.20000,12.90000.name: LOM's List Under Regulation
30.20000,12.90000.type: organism not named in the title, national biosafety decision
30.20000,12.90000.desc: A decision on a living modified organism, filed by the country itself to the Biosafety Clearing-House. Article 20 of the Cartagena Protocol requires every party to file its release and market decisions there within fifteen days, and 173 parties are bound by it. The United States is not among them. Nowhere else holds national release decisions from this many countries in one place. A country with no records here has not necessarily approved nothing — it may not have filed, and from the outside those two look the same.

-118.37700,34.06730.name: Center for Reproductive Health & Gynecology, (CRH&G)
-118.37700,34.06730.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Sam Najmabadi, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-77.15168,39.08180.name: Biomedical Research Institute
-77.15168,39.08180.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of American Foundation for Biological Research. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-1.47641,53.35827.name: CREATE Fertility Sheffield
-1.47641,53.35827.state: Sloan Medical Centre, 2 Little London Road, Meersbrook, Sheffield, S8 0YH
-1.47641,53.35827.company: Satellite clinic to CREATE Fertility, Leeds
-1.47641,53.35827.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to CREATE Fertility, Leeds. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-58.23424,-35.16707.name: FECUNDITAS
-58.23424,-35.16707.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: www.fecunditas.com / www.PGD-Fecunditas.com. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

-89.43000,43.07600.name: National Primate Research Centers (United States)
-89.43000,43.07600.desc: The US network of federally funded primate research facilities, holding thousands of monkeys for biomedical research including genetic modification. Primates are covered by the Animal Welfare Act, so unlike mice they are counted, and the numbers, procedures and inspection reports are public.

-122.00000,37.54000.name: Ultima Genomics
-122.00000,37.54000.desc: Announced sequencing at a cost far below the prevailing price, on a machine built around a spinning wafer rather than a flow cell. Whether or not it displaces Illumina, the announcement changed what buyers expect to pay — and the cost of reading a genome is the variable that decides whether population-scale programmes, newborn sequencing and routine embryo screening are affordable at all.

6.14000,46.22000.name: SGS — inspection and certification
6.14000,46.22000.desc: One of the largest inspection and certification companies in the world, testing and certifying agricultural cargoes at ports. A shipment is accepted or rejected on the strength of a private company’s certificate, which means a commercial testing firm sits between every exporting country and every import rule on this map. It also appears in market surveys of food certification alongside DEKRA, Intertek, Bureau Veritas, TÜV SÜD, Kiwa and Control Union, so the same firm certifies the organic and non-GM claim, runs the supervised field trial a regulator reads, and inspects the cargo at the port. Those are three roles this map treats as separate facets.

33.78000,-13.96000.name: Malawi Environmental Affairs Department — biosafety
33.78000,-13.96000.desc: Approved Bt cotton for commercial cultivation, one of the few African countries to reach commercial approval. Malawi is small, poor and landlocked, so its decision carries little weight commercially and considerable weight as precedent — which is roughly the reverse of how it is usually reported.
